q: Which Reddy king shifted his capital from Addanki to Kondavidu?
explanation: Anapota (Anavota) Reddi, elder son of Prolaya Vema, shifted the Reddi capital from Addanki to Kondavidu, as recorded in the Manyapuram inscription. Anavema, Kumaragiri and Pedakomati Vema ruled later from Kondavidu.

notes.text: - **Who shifted Addanki → Kondavidu:** **Anavota (Anapota) Reddi**, son of Prolaya Vema – **Manyapuram inscription** (APPSC G2 2012; PYQ) – not Anavema, Kumaragiri or Pedakomati.

q:
Arrange the following Reddi rulers in chronological order of their rule.

a. Prolaya Vema
b. Anavema
c. Anavotu Vema
d. Komaragiri
explanation: The Kondavidu order is Prolaya Vema (1325-53) → Anavota (1353-64) → Anavema (1364-86) → Komaragiri/Kumaragiri (1386-1402), i.e. a, c, b, d. Anavema came after Anavota, not before him.

notes.text: - **Order (APPSC G2 Mains 2025; Welfare Officers):** Prolaya Vema → **Anavota → Anavema → Kumaragiri → Pedakomati Vema** → Racha Vema.

q:
Arrange the following Reddi rulers chronologically:
A. Kumaragiri Reddi
B. Anavema Reddi
C. Anavota Reddi
D. Pedakomati Vema Reddi
explanation: Anavota (1353-64) → Anavema (1364-86) → Kumaragiri (1386-1402) → Pedakomati Vema (1402-20), i.e. C, B, A, D. Pedakomati Vema came last, after Kumaragiri died childless.

notes.text: - **Order (APPSC G2 Mains 2025; Welfare Officers):** Prolaya Vema → **Anavota → Anavema → Kumaragiri → Pedakomati Vema** → Racha Vema.

q: The literary work of the Reddy period which gives lot of information regarding the sea-borne trade is
explanation: Srinatha's Haravilasam, dedicated to the merchant Avachi Tippayya Setti, describes the imports, exports and sea-borne trade of the Reddi period (Motupalli). Kasikhandam, Bhimakhandam (Bhimeswara Puranam) are religious works and Harivamsa is Errana's.

notes.text: - **Haravilasam (Srinatha):** the Reddi-period work giving information on **sea-borne (foreign) trade**, imports and exports (APPSC G2 2011 ×2, 2012, 2019; G2 Mains; PYQ) – not Harivamsam, Kasikhandam or Bhimeswara Puranam.

q: Which was the popular religion during the time of the Reddy kings?
explanation: Veerashaivism was the popular religion of the Reddi period; the kings themselves patronised Pashupata Shaivism, which is the tempting wrong option.

notes.text: - **Popular religion:** **Veerashaivism** (APPSC G2 2011; PYQ); the kings patronised **Pashupata Shaivism** – the tempting wrong option.

q: Who built the Veerasiro Mandapam in Srisailam?
explanation: Anavema Reddi built the Veera Siromandapam at Srisailam (for Siro-karthanam devotees). Prolaya Vema built the steps to Patala Ganga there.
